summary: A one-joke microsite from MSCHF for a font that looks like Times New Roman but is 5–10% wider, so students can pad essays. Everything is staged as a comparison: an overlaid hero, a word-count face-off and two parallel sheets of paper. Black Times-style display with yellow as the second font's colour and Cousine for labels.

instances.look: About 2.5s full-screen black preloader with a rotating gradient frame (yellow, red, blue) around 'MSCHF DROP #03 / TIMES NEWER ROMAN'. It's the shared MSCHF preloader and wasn't cut as a block; seen only in the video (t<3s), attached to the first block
instances.ux: Plays once and fades over the hero; not skippable
instances.learn: Numbering each project as a 'drop' turns a font joke into a limited release, and a shared preloader brands a whole series of sites

reconstruction.layout: Fixed full-viewport black panel, ~6px coloured frame at the viewport edge, two centred lines
reconstruction.typography: ~14px serif uppercase; first line white, second red
reconstruction.behaviour: #gradientBackground rotates behind a slightly smaller black panel so the edge reads as a turning gradient frame; fades out at ~2.6s; classes preloader-hidden, preloader-remove

instances.look: 'One of these lines is longer than the other.' at ~190px, set twice on top of each other: black Times New Roman over yellow Times Newer Roman, the misregistration growing along each line; below, a black and a yellow label button
instances.ux: The two labels are radio labels, presumably switching which font is on top (the CSS is not in the archive). The overlap itself is the demo
instances.learn: Overprint the font on its rival in two colours: the drift along each line is the entire product pitch, with no need for a body sentence

reconstruction.layout: Container 1296px at x=72, top 60px; two absolutely stacked SVGs (viewBox 1177×568) scaled to the container, three lines ~175px apart with ~190 unit type; button row below, label buttons left and Download right
reconstruction.typography: Display ~190 SVG units (≈210px at 1440) Times New Roman and Times Newer Roman Regular, tight leading; labels 14px Cousine with 'Newer' in Bold, on black or yellow
reconstruction.behaviour: Hidden input.fonts radios #newer and #new (default newer) with label.button_newer and label.button_new; CSS sibling selectors likely restack or recolour the SVG layers (not verified). No scroll or ambient motion
reconstruction.content: The sentence is both a claim and a riddle
reconstruction.html: .row.compare > input.fonts[type=radio]#newer + input#new + .hero > svg#hero text.one-new + svg#hero-newer text.two-newer; label.button_newer, label.button_new

instances.look: Black 'Download Times Newer Roman' button at the right end of the hero's button row, with a tiny 'License info, project by MSCHF' and an SMS opt-in note below (those lines fall outside the block crop)
instances.ux: Direct ZIP download with a pixel tracking event; small print says using the project opts you in to texts
instances.learn: Keep the download in the hero when the idea is fully explained by the hero

reconstruction.layout: Button right aligned in the hero row, ~180×36px; small print centred under it, 12px, with a full-width 1px rule below
reconstruction.typography: Button 14px Cousine white on black with 'Newer' Bold; small print 12px Times Newer Roman with underlined Cousine links
reconstruction.content: 'License info, project by MSCHF', 'This is MSCHF drop #3. Text 917-540-3113 to get MSCHF drop #4 before the public.'

instances.look: Two short paragraphs at ~24px in Times Newer Roman at left: 'Introducing Times Newer Roman, a font that looks just like Times New Roman, except each character is 5-10% wider'
instances.learn: One sentence naming a real, shameful student problem is a complete brief: 'Fulfill lengthy page requirements with hacked margins, adjusted punctuation sizing, and now…'

reconstruction.layout: Full-width 1px rule on top; left column ~720px from x=72, ~250px tall, right column holds the diagram
reconstruction.typography: ~24px Times Newer Roman Regular, leading ~1.5, name in Bold
reconstruction.content: The product definition and the use case

instances.look: 'fml' in yellow fill (one font) overlaid with a black outline (the other); a dimension bar below labelled 'Much space'
instances.feel: Joke disguised as an engineering drawing
instances.learn: Hide a joke in the specimen word (fml), and use a drafting dimension line with a comic label to parody technical specimens

reconstruction.layout: Right column ~450px wide; word ~200px tall; dimension bar 440px wide below with end ticks; caption centred under it
reconstruction.typography: 'fml' ~411 SVG units in Times New Roman (outline, stroke 2) and yellow-filled Times Newer Roman; caption 12px Cousine

instances.variantDefinition: Two big figures side by side, each set in its own typeface under a label, stating one measured result of the comparison (word count, pages, file size), with a small badge giving the gain
instances.look: White panel: 'Estimated word count for a 15-page, single-spaced document in 12pt type:' over 6,680 in light Times New Roman and 5,833 in bold Times Newer Roman, divided by a vertical rule, with a yellow circular sticker 'A word savings of 13%!'
instances.learn: Reduce the claim to one measured number per font: set each number in its own font so the digits are also the sample

reconstruction.layout: White card 1296×484px at x=72 on grey; prompt centred on top; two columns ~350px wide split by a 1px vertical rule ~220px tall; each a grey label bar (~350×40px) above a number; sticker 88px circle right of the second number
reconstruction.typography: Prompt ~28px Times Regular; label 14px Cousine with 'Newer' Bold; numbers 112px Times New Roman Regular and Times Newer Roman Bold; sticker 12px Cousine, rotated ~-8°
reconstruction.content: 'Times New Roman 6,680', 'Times Newer Roman 5,833', 'A word savings of 13%!'

instances.variantDefinition: The same running text set in both typefaces on two side-by-side sheets at the same size, with no controls; the difference is read from where the text ends on each page
instances.look: 'Side-by-side comparison.' over two white paper sheets with black label bars ('Times New Roman / 14px', 'Times Newer Roman / 14px'); the right text runs a line or so longer
instances.ux: Static; the copy itself explains the method, and the punchline 'Brevity is the soul of wit.' closes both pages. Hidden on mobile, where the sheets are removed
instances.learn: Make the comparison copy the actual design notes: reading the sample teaches the changes (x-height +5%, punctuation +15%), and the end of the text marks the result

reconstruction.layout: Container 1296px; centred heading; two col-sm-4 sheets ~470×575px, 60px apart, 1px black border with a soft shadow, 28px padding
reconstruction.typography: Heading 28px Times Regular; label 14px Cousine white on a black bar; sample 14px at leading ~1.45 in Times New Roman and Times Newer Roman
reconstruction.content: The design note: an altered Nimbus Roman No.9 L, widened letters and gaps without changing heights, x-height +5%, punctuation +15%, 'hopefully without being noticeable to whoever's job it is to grade the paper.'

instances.look: Black strip with one centred Cousine line: 'Times Newer Roman is a MSCHF project. Text 917-540-3113 to hear about drops 24 hours early.'
